title: DatePicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.DatePickerDialog with androidx.compose.material3.DatePicker and androidx.compose.material3.rememberDatePickerState, inside MonarchFormField; MonarchMenu for presets
summary: The Material 3 date picker, opened in a DatePickerDialog from a button in a MonarchFormField row, with presets in a MonarchMenu beside it. The theme gives it Monarch colors, type and shapes; Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For one date in a form: a due date, a birthday, a start date. Use the inline DatePicker when the calendar is the main content of a sheet.
whenNotToUse: For a range, use the Material 3 DateRangePicker (see date-range-picker). For a calendar with per-day dots or disabled days and week numbers, use MonarchMiniMonth. For a time, use the Material 3 TimePicker.
api: @Composable fun DatePickerDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, confirmButton: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, dismissButton: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, shape: Shape = DatePickerDefaults.shape, …, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun DatePicker(state: DatePickerState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, dateFormatter: DatePickerFormatter = remember { DatePickerDefaults.dateFormatter() }, colors: DatePickerColors = DatePickerDefaults.colors(), title: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = …, headline: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = …, showModeToggle: Boolean = true, …)

@Composable fun rememberDatePickerState(initialSelectedDateMillis: Long? = null, initialDisplayedMonthMillis: Long? = initialSelectedDateMillis, yearRange: IntRange = DatePickerDefaults.YearRange, initialDisplayMode: DisplayMode = DisplayMode.Picker, selectableDates: SelectableDates = DatePickerDefaults.AllDates): DatePickerState
interface SelectableDates { fun isSelectableDate(utcTimeMillis: Long): Boolean; fun isSelectableYear(year: Int): Boolean }
@Composable fun MonarchFormField(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, …, control: @Composable (controlModifier: Modifier) -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, offset: DpOffset = DpOffset(MonarchTokens.Space.space0.dp, MonarchTokens.Space.space1.dp), content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

states.name: set
states.description: The field's button shows the date in the locale's medium format; tapping it opens the dialog with the date selected.

states.name: limited
states.description: Days that SelectableDates rejects are dimmed and cannot be chosen; yearRange limits the years.

states.name: optional
states.description: The app keeps a Long? and shows "Set date" and a Clear button; the picker itself always offers a date.

states.name: invalid
states.description: MonarchFormField shows the app's errorText with its icon under the row.

states.name: disabled
states.description: MonarchFormField(enabled = false) and a disabled button; the dialog cannot open.

states.name: input mode
states.description: The dialog's mode toggle switches to typing the date in the locale's pattern, validated by Material 3.

appearance: The dialog uses the raised surface with the extra-large corners, the selected day in the accent solid role with its on-solid text, today outlined in the accent role and disabled days in the disabled text role, all from MonarchTheme in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DatePicker is a typed field with a calendar popover, ISO string values, presets, min and max, disabled days, week numbers and field errors. On Android the Material 3 picker is the expected control: it formats and parses in the person's locale, and its input mode validates typed dates. min and max become SelectableDates and yearRange; presets are a MonarchMenu next to the field; an optional date needs a Long? in the app. Values are epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight (DatePickerState.selectedDateMillis): format them with a UTC formatter and store them as a day (yyyy-MM-dd) when they must not shift with time zones. Week numbers and per-day information are not offered by the Material 3 picker; for those, show MonarchMiniMonth in a sheet. iOS uses the SwiftUI DatePicker in the same MonarchFormField row.
accessibility: System behavior: the dialog is a window with its own title, so TalkBack moves into it and returns to the button when it closes.
System behavior: each day is a button read with its full date and whether it is selected or today; disabled days are read as disabled.
The field's button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target, labelled by MonarchFormField, and its text says the date or "Set date".
Font scale and right-to-left calendars are handled by Material 3.
edgeCases: selectedDateMillis is a UTC midnight: formatting it in the device zone can show the previous day west of UTC.
Remembering the state with the date as initialSelectedDateMillis keeps the dialog in step with presets only if the app also sets state.selectedDateMillis.
The dialog is tall; at the largest font scale on a small phone it scrolls.

The inline DatePicker is a fixed 360dp wide and cannot shrink: in a 320dp window the Saturday column is cut off. Draw it in a layout that scales it down to the space, as Monarch does in its own date dialogs; the scaled day cells are then 43dp wide.

examples.title: Due date with quick picks
examples.template:
MonarchFormField(label = {{label}}, helperText = {{helper}} + " Value: " + (due?.let { format.format(Date(it)) } ?: "none")) { controlModifier ->
    MonarchTextField(
        value = due?.let { format.format(Date(it)) } ?: "",
        onValueChange = {},
        modifier = controlModifier,
        placeholder = "DD/MM/YYYY",
        trailingIcon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Calendar, contentDescription = null, size = MonarchIconSize.Sm) },
    )
}
Column(
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxWidth()
        .clip(MonarchTheme.shapes.lg)
        .background(MonarchTheme.colors.bgSurface)
        .border(1.dp, MonarchTheme.colors.borderDefault, MonarchTheme.shapes.lg)
        .padding(MonarchTheme.spacing.space2),
) {
    presetList.forEach { (label, days) ->
        val day = today + days * 86_400_000L
        Row(
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().clickable { due = day }.padding(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3),
            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
        ) {
            MonarchText(text = label)
            MonarchText(text = dayFormat.format(Date(day)), style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption, color = MonarchTheme.colors.textMuted)
        }
    }
    DatePicker(
        state = state,
        title = null,
        headline = null,
        showModeToggle = false,
        colors = DatePickerDefaults.colors(
            todayContentColor = MonarchTheme.colors.textDefault,
            todayDateBorderColor = Color.Transparent,
        ),
    )
}
